GoGrameen
Moderator Dashboard — Feature Spec  v2.0
9 features  ·  47 tasks  ·  9 sample UI screens  ·  gogrameen.in/moderator

Features

Version
2.0 · May 2025



1. What is the Moderator?
The Moderator is a trusted local person — assigned by the GoGrameen founders — who manages the farmer-consumer ecosystem in a specific geographic zone. For the first 3 months, the founders themselves will act as the moderator for the Tadepalligudem zone.

Onboards new farmers in their zone (especially farmers who cannot use smartphones)
Reviews and approves farmer listings before they go live on the consumer page
Monitors supply vs demand and recruits farmers to fill gaps
Handles escalations — delivery delays, quality complaints, payment issues
Manages delivery agents — registers, monitors, activates/deactivates
Sets suggested price ranges per crop so new farmers price sensibly

ℹ  Route: /moderator (or /moderator/dashboard). Login required. Role = "moderator" in the Supabase profiles table. A moderator only sees data for their assigned zone.

1.1  All 9 features at a glance
#
Feature
What it does
1
Dashboard home
Summary stats, alert strip, and quick-action shortcuts
2
Farmer onboarding
Register farmers, generate profile links, share via WhatsApp
3
Listing management
Approve, edit, or reject farmer produce listings
4
Supply vs demand
Live crop balance table with demand vs supply bars
5
Consumer management
View buyers, buying patterns, and demand intents
6
Delivery agent management
Onboard and manage local delivery agents
7
Escalation management
View, progress, and resolve complaints
8
Price management
Set suggested price ranges per crop for the zone
9
Reports
Weekly/monthly zone performance with PDF export



2. Feature specifications
  Feature 1     Dashboard home
The first screen when the moderator logs in. Instant snapshot of zone health — stat cards, an alert strip, and quick-action buttons.

Screen contents
Header: moderator name, zone name, today's date
Alert strip: red if open escalations or pending approvals exist; amber if any crop is scarce; green if all is well
Six stat cards: Active farmers, Consumers, Orders this week, GMV this week, Open escalations (red if > 0), Pending approvals (amber if > 0)
Quick action buttons: "Onboard a farmer", "Review listings", "View escalations", "View reports"


Feature 1 — Dashboard home: stat cards, alert strip, and quick-action buttons
Developer tasks
Task ID
Task name
What to build
How (for a fresher)
MOD-1.1
Moderator login & route protection
Build /moderator/login with phone OTP. Check role = "moderator" in profiles table before showing the dashboard.
Use Supabase Auth phone OTP (same as farmer login). After login, query SELECT role FROM profiles WHERE id = auth.uid(). If role != "moderator", redirect to /consumer.
MOD-1.2
Dashboard header
Show moderator name, zone name, and today's date.
Query the moderators table for the logged-in user. Display name and region_slug. Use new Date().toLocaleDateString("en-IN") for the date.
MOD-1.3
Alert strip logic
Red if escalations open > 0 OR pending listings > 0. Amber if any crop is scarce. Green otherwise.
Run two queries on load: (1) COUNT escalations WHERE status = "open", (2) COUNT listings WHERE status = "pending_review". If either > 0 → red. Else check supply_demand view for scarce rows → amber.
MOD-1.4
Six stat cards
Six live numbers from the database.
Write one Supabase query per card. All filter by region_slug = moderator's zone. For GMV: SELECT SUM(total_price) FROM orders WHERE created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL "7 days".
MOD-1.5
Quick action buttons
Three buttons that navigate to specific sections.
Use Next.js router.push(). No API needed. Button 1 → /moderator/farmers/new. Button 2 → /moderator/listings. Button 3 → /moderator/escalations.



  Feature 2     Farmer onboarding
The most immediately useful feature. Moderator registers new farmers on their behalf, and the system generates a shareable profile link.

Screen contents
List of all farmers in zone with name, village, method badge, listing count, status, and Edit button
"+ Add new farmer" button opens a registration form
Form fields: name, phone, village, district, farming method, farm size, farming since year, story quote, crops, water source, farm visit day, pickup availability, bank account + IFSC
On save: auto-generate slug from name, create profile at /farmer/{slug}, show "Share via WhatsApp" button


Feature 2 — Farmer onboarding: farmer list and registration form
Developer tasks
Task ID
Task name
What to build
How (for a fresher)
MOD-2.1
Farmer list page
/moderator/farmers — table of all farmers in the zone.
Query farmers WHERE region_slug = moderator's zone. Show name, village, method (as badge), listing count (subquery), active status.
MOD-2.2
Add farmer form
/moderator/farmers/new — all fields listed above.
POST /api/moderator/farmers. Insert into farmers table. Return new farmer's id and slug.
MOD-2.3
Auto-generate slug
Create URL-safe slug from the farmer's name on save.
name.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, "-").replace(/^-|-$/g, ""). Check if slug exists; append "-2" if taken.
MOD-2.4
WhatsApp share after save
Show success screen with profile URL and share button.
Build wa.me link: wa.me/91{phone}?text=Your farm page is live: gogrameen.in/farmer/{slug}. Open in new tab on tap.
MOD-2.5
Edit & activate/deactivate
Edit farmer details and toggle active status.
Re-use the form with pre-filled data. PATCH /api/moderator/farmers/[id] for updates. Toggle active field on the list view.
MOD-2.6
Secure bank details
Store account number and IFSC. Show only last 4 digits.
Store plain in Supabase (RLS: only moderator + admin can read). Display: account.slice(-4).padStart(account.length, "*").



  Feature 3     Listing management
Every farmer listing goes through the moderator for approval before appearing on the consumer page. This keeps listing quality high and prevents pricing errors.

Screen contents
Three tabs: Pending approval (amber count badge), Active listings, Rejected
Each pending card: produce name, farmer, method, price, stock, BRIX, date submitted
Per card actions: Approve (green), Reject (coral — requires reason text), Edit before approving
On approve: status → available, consumer page shows listing, farmer gets WhatsApp
On reject: status → rejected, farmer gets WhatsApp with the rejection reason


Feature 3 — Listing management: pending listing cards with approve/reject actions
Developer tasks
Task ID
Task name
What to build
How (for a fresher)
MOD-3.1
Pending listings tab
All listings WHERE status = "pending_review" in the zone.
JOIN produce_listings with farmers WHERE farmers.region_slug = zone AND status = "pending_review". Sort by created_at ASC (oldest first).
MOD-3.2
Approve a listing
PATCH status to "available". Notify farmer via WhatsApp.
PATCH /api/moderator/listings/[id] → { status: "available" }. After DB update, trigger Twilio WhatsApp to farmer: "Your {produce} listing is live!".
MOD-3.3
Reject with reason
Modal with required textarea. Save reason. Notify farmer.
Show a modal div (not window.alert). On confirm: PATCH listing with { status: "rejected", rejection_reason: text }. WhatsApp farmer with the reason.
MOD-3.4
Edit before approving
Pre-filled form to fix errors before approving.
Re-use the produce listing form component. Pre-fill from listing data. Save keeps status = "pending_review". Moderator then approves.
MOD-3.5
Active listings management
View and suspend any active listing.
Show active listings tab. Add Suspend button → sets status = "sold_out". Show all details including farmer name.
MOD-3.6
Add rejection_reason column
DB change needed.
In Supabase SQL editor: ALTER TABLE produce_listings ADD COLUMN rejection_reason TEXT;



  Feature 4     Supply vs demand monitor
The strategic heart of the moderator dashboard. Shows which crops are short, balanced, or in surplus — and lets the moderator act immediately.

Screen contents
Table: Crop | Demand (kg) | Supply (kg) | Gap (+/-) | Status | Action
Status colours: OK (green) / Low (amber) / Scarce (red) / Surplus (teal)
Bar chart below: orange = demand bar, green = supply bar, side by side per crop
"Notify farmers" button next to each Scarce row — sends WhatsApp to all farmers in the zone who grow that crop


Feature 4 — Supply vs demand: crop balance table and comparison bars
Developer tasks
Task ID
Task name
What to build
How (for a fresher)
MOD-4.1
Supply & demand data
Aggregate demand from intents and supply from active listings.
Two Supabase queries: (1) SELECT crop_name, SUM(quantity_kg) FROM demand_intents WHERE region_slug = zone GROUP BY crop_name. (2) SELECT name, SUM(stock_qty) FROM produce_listings WHERE status = "available" GROUP BY name. Merge in JS.
MOD-4.2
Status colour logic
Calculate status from supply and demand numbers.
In JS: if supply >= demand → "OK". Else if supply >= demand*0.5 → "Low". Else if supply < demand*0.5 → "Scarce". Else if supply > demand*1.5 → "Surplus". Apply Tailwind badge class.
MOD-4.3
Bar chart
Demand vs supply bars per crop using Chart.js.
new Chart(canvas, { type: "bar", data: { labels: cropNames, datasets: [{ label: "Demand", data: demandArray, backgroundColor: "#EF9F27" }, { label: "Supply", data: supplyArray, backgroundColor: "#4A8A2D" }] } })
MOD-4.4
Notify farmers button
WhatsApp message to all farmers in zone who grow the scarce crop.
POST /api/moderator/notify-scarce with { crop_name }. Query farmers in zone whose crops_raw ILIKE "%{crop_name}%". Build Twilio WhatsApp call for each.



  Feature 5     Consumer management
The moderator sees all buyers in their zone plus all open demand intents — unmet requests waiting to be fulfilled.


Feature 5 — Consumer management: top buyers list and open demand intents
Developer tasks
Task ID
Task name
What to build
How (for a fresher)
MOD-5.1
Consumer list
All consumers who have ordered in the zone.
SELECT consumers.name, consumers.location, COUNT(orders.id) as order_count, SUM(orders.total_price) as total_spend FROM orders JOIN consumers WHERE farmer_id IN (farmers in zone) GROUP BY consumer_id. Sort by total_spend DESC.
MOD-5.2
Demand intents list
Open intents in the zone sorted by urgency.
SELECT * FROM demand_intents WHERE region_slug = zone AND fulfilled = false ORDER BY needed_by_date ASC.
MOD-5.3
Mark intent fulfilled
Button on each intent. Sets fulfilled = true. Notifies consumer.
PATCH /api/moderator/demand-intents/[id] with { fulfilled: true }. WhatsApp to requester_phone: "Good news! {crop} is now available. Order here: gogrameen.in/consumer".



  Feature 6     Delivery agent management
Moderator recruits and manages local delivery agents — bike owners or anyone who wants to earn extra income by delivering farm produce.


Feature 6 — Delivery agent management: agent list with performance stats
Developer tasks
Task ID
Task name
What to build
How (for a fresher)
MOD-6.1
Agents list
/moderator/agents — table of all agents in the zone.
Query delivery_agents WHERE zone = moderator's zone. Join with deliveries to get completed count per agent.
MOD-6.2
Add agent form
Register new agent — name, phone, vehicle, availability.
POST /api/moderator/agents. Insert into delivery_agents. Fields: name, phone, aadhaar_hash (hash the Aadhaar, never store plain), vehicle_type, availability, zone.
MOD-6.3
Activate/deactivate
Toggle active status.
PATCH /api/moderator/agents/[id] with { active: false }. Inactive agents do not appear in the delivery dashboard pickups.
MOD-6.4
Create delivery_agents table
New DB table.
CREATE TABLE delivery_agents (id uuid PK, name varchar(100), phone varchar(15), aadhaar_hash text, vehicle_type text, availability text[], zone varchar(60), active boolean default true, created_at timestamptz)



  Feature 7     Escalation management
Complaints from farmers or consumers — and auto-detected issues like delivery delays — are tracked here. The moderator investigates and resolves each one.


Feature 7 — Escalations: open complaints with in-progress and resolved states
Developer tasks
Task ID
Task name
What to build
How (for a fresher)
MOD-7.1
Escalations list
All escalations in zone sorted by date.
Query escalations WHERE region_slug = zone ORDER BY created_at DESC. Show type badge, description, order link, raised-by, status.
MOD-7.2
Status update
Mark in-progress or resolved. Resolved requires notes.
PATCH /api/moderator/escalations/[id]. For resolved: { status: "resolved", resolution_notes: text, resolved_at: new Date() }.
MOD-7.3
Notify on resolution
When resolved, WhatsApp both farmer and consumer.
After PATCH, read order's farmer_id and consumer phone. Send WhatsApp to both with the resolution notes.
MOD-7.4
Auto-create delivery delay
If delivery in_transit > 6 hours, create escalation.
Supabase Edge Function running every 30 min: SELECT id FROM deliveries WHERE status = "in_transit" AND picked_up_at < NOW() - INTERVAL "6 hours". For each, INSERT into escalations if not exists.
MOD-7.5
DB changes
Add columns to escalations table.
ALTER TABLE escalations ADD COLUMN resolution_notes TEXT; ALTER TABLE escalations ADD COLUMN resolved_at TIMESTAMPTZ;



  Feature 8     Price management
Suggested price ranges per crop for the zone. Shown as hint text on the farmer listing form — guidance only, not enforced.


Feature 8 — Price management: editable price range table per crop
Developer tasks
Task ID
Task name
What to build
How (for a fresher)
MOD-8.1
Create price_guidelines table
New DB table.
CREATE TABLE price_guidelines (id uuid PK, crop_name varchar(100), region_slug varchar(60), min_price numeric(8,2), max_price numeric(8,2), unit varchar(20) DEFAULT 'kg', updated_at timestamptz, updated_by uuid)
MOD-8.2
Price table UI
/moderator/prices — editable table, one row per crop.
Fetch price_guidelines WHERE region_slug = zone. Each row has two <input type="number"> fields for min and max. Clicking into a field enables editing.
MOD-8.3
Auto-save on blur
Save when moderator clicks out of a price field.
input onBlur → PATCH /api/moderator/prices/[id] with new value. Show a brief "Saved ✓" confirmation text next to the field for 2 seconds.
MOD-8.4
Hint on farmer form
Show suggested range when farmer enters produce name.
On farmer listing form, when produce name changes: GET /api/prices?crop={name}&region={zone}. If found, show helper text under price field: "Suggested: ₹{min}–₹{max}/kg".



  Feature 9     Reports
Weekly and monthly zone performance. The moderator reviews this to understand trends; founders use it to evaluate zone growth.


Feature 9 — Reports: period selector, KPI cards, top farmer, most popular crop
Developer tasks
Task ID
Task name
What to build
How (for a fresher)
MOD-9.1
Period toggle
Three buttons: This week / This month / Last month.
useState({ period: "week" }). Each button updates state. Compute startDate and endDate from the period value. Pass to all API calls.
MOD-9.2
KPI queries
Orders, GMV, avg order value, escalation resolution rate.
GET /api/moderator/reports?region=zone&from=DATE&to=DATE. SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) as orders, SUM(total_price) as gmv, AVG(total_price) as avg_order FROM orders WHERE created_at BETWEEN from AND to.
MOD-9.3
Top farmer & most popular crop
Who sold most and which crop moved most.
SELECT farmer_id, SUM(total_price) as gmv FROM orders GROUP BY farmer_id ORDER BY gmv DESC LIMIT 1. For crop: SELECT produce_name, COUNT(*) FROM order_items GROUP BY produce_name ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1.
MOD-9.4
PDF export
Download the current report as a PDF.
Add @media print CSS: hide sidebar and nav, show only the report content. Call window.print() when the Download button is tapped. Browser renders a printable PDF.



3. Database additions
Run all of these in Supabase SQL editor before starting development.

3.1  New tables
delivery_agents
CREATE TABLE delivery_agents (
  id            uuid DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() PRIMARY KEY,
  name          varchar(100) NOT NULL,
  phone         varchar(15) NOT NULL,
  aadhaar_hash  text,
  vehicle_type  text,
  delivery_area text,
  availability  text[],
  zone          varchar(60),

);

price_guidelines

  id           uuid DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() PRIMARY KEY,
  crop_name    varchar(100) NOT NULL,
  region_slug  varchar(60) NOT NULL,
  min_price    numeric(8,2),
  max_price    numeric(8,2),

  updated_at   timestamptz DEFAULT now()
);

-- Moderators read only their own zone's farmers
CREATE POLICY "moderator_zone_farmers" ON farmers FOR SELECT

I've gone through the full spec text you pasted plus all 8 pages of `moderator.pdf`. The two HTML files are just the Google Docs export of the same spec, so they're duplicates of the text. Here's what's actually inside it all.

## What this is

The client sent you a **Moderator Dashboard spec (v2.0)** — a brand-new, separate section of GoGrameen/YourFamilyFarmer. It's a **private admin-style area** that only a "moderator" can see. Farmers, consumers, and delivery boys are explicitly locked out of it.

- **Route:** `/moderator` (or `/moderator/dashboard`), login required
- **Access control:** only users with `role = "moderator"` in the Supabase `profiles` table get in; everyone else is redirected to `/consumer`
- **Scope:** a moderator only sees data for **their own zone** (first zone = Tadepalligudem, run by the founders for the first 3 months)

A moderator is a trusted local person who onboards farmers (especially non-smartphone ones), approves listings before they go live, watches supply vs demand, handles complaints, manages delivery agents, and sets suggested prices.

## The 8 PDF pages = real UI mockups of the screens

The PDF isn't more text — it's **screenshots of the actual designed dashboard** (dark green sidebar, "Tadepalligudem zone" badge top-right). Each page matches a feature in the spec:

| PDF page | Screen | What it shows |
|---|---|---|

Here's the **exact role of the Moderator**, pulled straight from this spec.

## Who the Moderator is

A **trusted local person, hand-picked by the GoGrameen founders**, who runs the entire farmer–consumer ecosystem for **one geographic zone**. Think of them as the **on-ground zone manager / gatekeeper** — not a farmer, not a consumer, not a delivery agent, but the person who supervises all of them in their area.

- First zone: **Tadepalligudem**
- First 3 months: **the founders themselves are the moderator** (until they train a local person to take over)
- They **only see and control their own zone** — never other zones' data

## Their 6 core responsibilities

| # | What they do | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Onboard farmers** — including farmers who can't use a smartphone | The moderator registers them on their behalf and creates their `/farmer/{slug}` page |
| 2 | **Approve / reject listings** before they go live | They are the **quality gate** — no farmer produce reaches the consumer page until the moderator approves it |
| 3 | **Monitor supply vs demand** and recruit farmers to fill gaps | If mangoes are scarce, they nudge farmers to grow/list more |
| 4 | **Handle escalations** — delivery delays, quality complaints, payment issues | They are the **complaint resolver** for their zone |
| 5 | **Manage delivery agents** — register, monitor, activate/deactivate | They run the local delivery workforce |
| 6 | **Set suggested price ranges per crop** | So new farmers price sensibly (guidance only, not enforced) |

## The key thing to understand about the role

The moderator is essentially a **human trust-and-quality layer** sitting between farmers and consumers. The platform deliberately does **not** auto-publish farmer listings or let complaints go unmanaged — a real person reviews and controls it all, zone by zone.

Three powers define the role:

1. **Gatekeeper** — nothing reaches buyers without their approval (listings).
2. **Recruiter / balancer** — they actively shape supply to match demand and pull in new farmers + delivery agents.
3. **Dispute resolver** — every complaint in the zone lands on their desk to investigate and close.

## What this means technically (access)

- Logs in at `/moderator` via **phone OTP**
- Must have `role = "moderator"` in the `profiles` table — anyone else is bounced to `/consumer`
- **RLS locks them to their own `region_slug`** — they physically cannot read or edit another zone's farmers/listings
- This area is **completely invisible** to farmers, consumers, and delivery agents

## One distinction worth noting

The spec separates the **moderator** from the **founders**:
- **Moderator** = day-to-day operator of one zone (onboarding, approvals, complaints)
- **Founders** = use the **Reports** feature (Feature 9) to evaluate zone growth from above

For now those are the same people, but the design assumes they'll eventually be different — a moderator running the ground game, founders watching the numbers across zones.

So in one sentence: **the Moderator is the founder-appointed local zone manager who onboards and curates farmers, approves what buyers see, balances supply and demand, manages delivery agents, and resolves all complaints — strictly within their assigned zone.**

I've now got the full picture of how your app actually works — and there's one important thing you should know before we build: **your real codebase does auth differently from what the moderator spec assumes.**

## How your app actually gates roles today

You don't use Supabase Auth + a `role` column (that's what the PDF spec assumes). Instead, each role has its **own separate signed cookie**, and the sections are naturally invisible to each other:

| Role | URL | Cookie | How they log in |
|------|-----|--------|-----------------|
| Consumer | `/consumer` | `yff_consumer` | phone session |
| Farmer | `/farmer/dashboard` | `yff_farmer` | login |
| Rider (delivery) | `/rider/dashboard` | `yff_rider` | login |
| Admin/Owner | `/admin` | `yff_admin` | single `ADMIN_PASSWORD` |

The HMAC for each cookie is namespaced (`admin:`, `rider:`, …), so **a farmer/consumer/rider token literally cannot be replayed against another role's routes.** A logged-in farmer hitting `/moderator` just gets bounced to login — exactly the isolation you want.

So **yes, we can absolutely add a `/moderator` section that farmers, consumers, and delivery agents cannot see.** The clean way is to copy your existing `admin` pattern, *not* the spec's Supabase-OTP approach (that infrastructure — `profiles.role`, moderator OTP — doesn't exist in your app, so following the PDF literally would mean building a whole second auth system).

## The one decision I need from you

How should a moderator log in? This is the only real fork in the road:

4	// HMAC-signed session token (server-only). Stored in an HTTP-only cookie so
5	// XSS cannot exfiltrate it. Format: <consumerId>.<issuedAtMs>.<hmacHexBase64url>
6	//
7	// We never put consumer name or phone in the token — those live in the DB.
8	// localStorage holds the public profile copy used purely for UI display, and

11	const COOKIE_NAME = 'yff_consumer'
12	const TOKEN_TTL_MS = 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000 // 30 days
13	
14	export function getSessionSecret(): string {
15	  const secret = process.env.SESSION_SECRET
16	  if (!secret || secret.length < 32) {
17	    throw new Error(
18	      'SESSION_SECRET env var is missing or too short. Set a 32+ char random string in your environment (e.g. `openssl rand -hex 32`).',
19	    )
20	  }
21	  return secret
22	}

24	function b64url(buf: Buffer): string {
25	  return buf.toString('base64').replace(/\+/g, '-').replace(/\//g, '_').replace(/=+$/, '')
26	}
27	
28	function sign(payload: string): string {
29	  const secret = getSessionSecret()
30	  return b64url(createHmac('sha256', secret).update(payload).digest())
31	}
32	
33	export function createSessionToken(consumerId: string): string {
34	  const issuedAt = Date.now()
35	  const payload = `${consumerId}.${issuedAt}`
36	  const sig = sign(payload)
37	  return `${payload}.${sig}`
38	}
39	
40	export type SessionPayload = { consumerId: string; issuedAt: number }
41	
42	export function verifySessionToken(token: string | undefined | null): SessionPayload | null {
43	  if (!token) return null
44	  const parts = token.split('.')
45	  if (parts.length !== 3) return null
46	  const [consumerId, issuedAtStr, sig] = parts
47	  const issuedAt = Number(issuedAtStr)
48	  if (!consumerId || !Number.isFinite(issuedAt)) return null
49	  if (Date.now() - issuedAt > TOKEN_TTL_MS) return null
50	
51	  let expected: string
52	  try {
53	    expected = sign(`${consumerId}.${issuedAtStr}`)
54	  } catch {
55	    return null
56	  }
57	  const a = Buffer.from(sig)
58	  const b = Buffer.from(expected)
59	  if (a.length !== b.length) return null
60	  if (!timingSafeEqual(a, b)) return null
61	  return { consumerId, issuedAt }
62	}
63	
64	export function getConsumerSessionFromRequest(req: NextRequest): SessionPayload | null {
65	  const token = req.cookies.get(COOKIE_NAME)?.value
66	  return verifySessionToken(token)
67	}
